title: No Deletion Without Understanding — The Preservation Law

source.source_reference: Shawn Vibert (Human Director), 2026-10-05, main chat. Standing directive after the deletion and restoration of SN-0358 and SN-0359: understand what an artifact is, what purpose it serves, and whether it is important or load-bearing before any deletion or destructive cleanup.

intelligence.essence: Never delete or destructively simplify intelligence until you understand what it is, what purpose it serves, what depends on it, and what authority governs its lifecycle. Optimization means improving the system, not reducing file count.

human_view.meaning: Before removing anything, understand it first. A file that looks duplicate, stale or messy may still carry law, provenance, identity, continuity or an active dependency.
human_view.why_it_matters: Cleanup without comprehension can destroy the very intelligence the system is meant to preserve. The cost of a false deletion is much higher than the cost of keeping an uncertain artifact while it is investigated.
human_view.simple_rule: Understand first. Trace purpose and dependencies. Preserve when uncertain. Delete only through an authorized lifecycle decision.

simple_view.child: Do not throw something away just because you do not recognize it. First find out what it is and why it is there.
simple_view.grandma: Before cleaning out the cupboard, check what everything is for. Important things can look like clutter if you have not understood them yet.

naya_view.purpose: Prevent optimization, deduplication and cleanup from erasing valuable or governed intelligence.
before_destructive_change: TRACE dependencies, references, provenance and authority
VERIFY replacement or supersession if applicable
CHECK authority for the destructive action
ACT only after all applicable gates pass
invalid_shortcuts: delete because cleanup would reduce file count
delete because another artifact seems similar

ai_view.instruction: Treat deletion as a governed lifecycle action, not a cleanup primitive. Never infer dispensability from naming, similarity, age, formatting defects, CI pressure or apparent duplication. Establish meaning, dependencies, provenance, replacement semantics and authority first. Prefer migrate, supersede, archive, deprecate or exclude from active retrieval over destructive deletion when those preserve intelligence.
ai_view.anti_pattern: Optimization-by-erasure: making the repository look cleaner by deleting artifacts whose semantic role has not been proven disposable.

decisions: Ratified laws and governance code are protected intelligence and may not be removed by ordinary cleanup or deduplication.
Semantic similarity is not deletion authority.
Formatting or schema defects must be repaired in place or through explicit supersession, not erased.
Unknown purpose or dependency means preserve and read more.
A destructive retirement requires explicit lifecycle evidence and applicable authority.
Mechanical tests should protect named critical intelligence from disappearance.

connections.target: a2f103f4 — deletion of SN-0358 and SN-0359 during Smart Note schema repair

intelligence.uncertainty: This law is ratified governing direction. Universal enforcement is not proven until the protected-intelligence registry and regression test demonstrate that deletion of a protected Smart Note makes the test suite fail.
intelligence.applicability: All Naya and Coda seats, automated cleanup, deduplication, migrations, repository maintenance, archival and any destructive intelligence lifecycle action.
intelligence.learning_lesson: The failure was not that cleanup exists; it was treating deletion as harmless before understanding semantic purpose and lifecycle authority. Clean systems come from correct classification and explicit lifecycle transitions, not indiscriminate file removal.
intelligence.successor_effect: A cold successor encountering a suspicious, duplicate-looking or malformed artifact first reconstructs its purpose, dependencies, authority and replacement path. If any of those are unknown, the successor preserves it and investigates instead of deleting it.
intelligence.falsifier: The protocol is falsified, or insufficient, if EITHER: (a) a seat follows this protocol and still deletes something critical, meaning the verification steps are insufficient; OR (b) the protocol measurably increases destructive hesitancy — seats failing to clean up genuinely redundant artifacts, or leaving dead weight in the working set — which would mean the gate is too blunt and is costing verified value; OR (c) it measurably increases false confidence about what is load-bearing, i.e. seats assert understanding without having it.
intelligence.measurement_contract: Measured as verified capability delta. CONTROL = pre-law baseline. TREATMENT = PRESERVATION-LAW-V1 active. Report both false negatives (critical deletions) AND false positives (over-preservation). Never measured by deletion count alone in either direction. Track confidence against correctness per SN-042.
